text:
maria: Alert from telemetry: multiple partner namespace secrets showing TTLs > 30d and active renewals. Looks like automation kept extending leases beyond policy. Link: https://internal/telemetry/alerts/TTL-ANOM-2026. @devin can you confirm?

devin: seeing the same. Grepped vault-audit logs: `jq '.request_id,.path,.lease_id,.renew' audit.log | grep partner-namespace` — found ~87 renew events after expiry.

maria: Oof. Could be a buggy cron or a rogue operator. Severity: medium-high until we confirm blast radius.

oliver: Create an incident and page sec-oncall. Also we should immediately enable extra audit hooks and snapshot the KMS key material metadata.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-2026-04-22-ttl-renewal. PagerDuty: sec-oncall paged.

maria: Quick containment suggestions: 1) disable the renewer automation (if identified) 2) revoke any long-lived tokens for partner clients 3) lift KMS key version to a new primary and rewrap ciphertexts 4) add RBAC deny for implicated SAs until we reprovision short-lived creds. Thoughts?

devin: Agreed. Step 1: identify automation - grep commit history for `partner-namespace-renewer` and check CRON jobs. Found a cronjob in infra-k8s: `partner-renewer` scheduled daily. I can pause it via `kubectl scale --replicas=0 deployment/partner-renewer -n infra`.

maria: Do it. Also capture current lease list: `vault list -format=json sys/leases/lookup | jq '.[] | select(.path|contains("partner-namespace"))' > partner_leases.json`

devin: paused deployment. Scaling to 0 done.

oliver: Before revoking tokens, we need a consumer list. Use telemetry to map lease->client: `cat partner_leases.json | jq -r '.[].lease_id' | xargs -I{} grep {} telemetry.log | cut -f1 -d' ' | sort -u`  — gives ~30 clients. I'll post the list to the incident channel.

sec-bot: Audit hook enabled: vault-audit-s3 for partner-namespace at debug. Stream: s3://redwood-audit/partner-namespace/2026-04-22-debug/

maria: OK plan: devin revoke automation paused; oliver assemble client list; i'll coordinate KMS rewrap + key rotation and the RBAC temporary deny. Need volunteers to run revokes and rewrap.

devin: I'll take revokes. Command: `vault token revoke -prefix=partner-namespace/lease_2026*` then validate with `vault token lookup -format=json <token>` for random samples. Running now.

devin: Update: revoked ~95 tokens. Some downstream jobs started failing (webhook 502s). Throttling and notifying infra teams.

oliver: Client list posted to incident doc. Notifying product partner ops to expect disruptions.

maria: For KMS rewrap: we'll create a new key version and re-encrypt wrapped blobs. Steps: 1) create key version (gcloud kms keys versions create) 2) set new version primary 3) re-encrypt blobs via streaming job that reads ciphertext from s3 and writes rewrapped ciphertext to s3 path `s3://redwood-encrypted/partner/rewrap/2026-04-22/`. Devin, can you run the rewrap job?

devin: I'll spin up a job. Script uses `gcloud kms decrypt --location=global --keyring=prod-wrap --key=partner-wrap --ciphertext-file=-` piped into encrypt to new key version. I'll run on a dedicated pool to avoid noisy-neighbor.

maria: Also open a terraform PR to add an explicit deny binding for `serviceAccount:partner-ingest@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with a temp TTL 1h. Use `google_service_account_iam_member` with role `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` but negative? We don't have negative bindings in IAM; instead create a condition to block usage or rotate keys and remove SA from members. Dev note: we can use OrganizationPolicy to deny iam.serviceAccounts.signBlob for that SA temporarily.

oliver: I'll draft the terraform change and mark it for urgent review. PR link: https://git.redwood/infra/PRs/9081 (WIP).

sec-bot: Noted vulnerability tag: potential exposure window > 24h. Recommend vulnerability triage board entry.

maria: Add to triage: check if any encrypted backups containing partner ciphertext were exported to partner buckets or third parties. Search S3 exports and partner transfer logs.

devin: Found one copied blob in `s3://partner-exports/2026-04-20/backup-partner-a.enc` — contacting legal and partner ops.

maria: Notify partner security immediately (do not call legal until we know scope). Draft message: short statement of suspected long-lived access, steps we took (revoked leases, paused renewal job, rewrapped data, rotated KMS version), and offer rotation timeline. I'll draft and post to #partner-ops for review.

oliver: Rewrap job started. At 15% progress now. No decryption errors yet.

devin: Revokes complete. Collected revoke audit: s3://redwood-audit/exports/revokes/2026-04-22.json.

maria: Rewrap complete and new key version set primary. Need to verify consumers can decrypt; schedule rolling restarts for affected services.

oliver: Restarted 5 consumer deployments; decrypt tests passed for smoke endpoints. Monitoring for 30m.

sec-bot: Incident INCIDENT-2026-04-22-ttl-renewal status: mitigated -> monitoring. PagerDuty incident status updated.

maria: Next steps (post-incident): 1) add gating check on partner onboarding to prevent automations from granting infinite renewals 2) implement auto-detect + auto-revoke for renewals beyond policy 3) add a KMS rewrap playbook to runbook repo 4) run a vuln triage meeting to review the export found in partner-exports bucket. Owners: devin (revocation automation), oliver (rewrap runbook), maria (partner comms + triage). Postmortem scheduled Mon 9am PT.

devin: I'll prototype auto-revoke lambda that watches for renewals > TTL and issues `vault token revoke` with a safe cooldown.

oliver: I'll commit the rewrap runbook and the terraform deny PR.

maria: Great. Closing the channel for this thread, move notes to postmortem doc. If anyone sees reproducing renewals re-enable pings. Thanks. :thumbsup:
